name: Eleazar
bio:
Eleazar is Aaron's third son, who became one of Aaron's two surviving sons after his elder brothers Nadab and Abihu were struck down by God for offering strange fire (Leviticus 10:6, 12). Moses was once angry at Eleazar and his brother Ithamar for not eating the sin offering meat in the holy place as instructed; Aaron explained the circumstances of that difficult day, and Moses was satisfied (Leviticus 10:16-20).

Eleazar's role grew increasingly important as Israel's journey under Moses continued toward Canaan, and after Aaron's death he succeeded him as Israel's second high priest — a story told in detail in the book of Numbers.

After Joshua led Israel into Canaan, Eleazar worked alongside him to apportion the land to the people by tribe (Joshua 14:1). Eleazar later died and was buried on a hill in the hill country of Ephraim that had been given to his son Phinehas (Joshua 24:33).
